title: Only Three Flexi-Cap Funds Earn Five Stars in July as Category Heats Up
excerpt: HDFC Flexi Cap, Parag Parikh Flexi Cap, and HDFC Retirement Savings stand alone at the top of Value Research's ratings, while newcomer Abakkus delivers strong early returns.
body:
• Value Research awarded five-star ratings to only three flexi-cap funds in July: HDFC Flexi Cap (27% three-year CAGR), Parag Parikh Flexi Cap (24.5%), and HDFC Retirement Savings Equity Plan (23-24%).
  • Parag Parikh Flexi Cap crossed Rs 1.48 lakh crore in assets under management, making selective additions to Petronet LNG (+52%) and CIE Automotive (+73%) in July.
  • Newcomer Abakkus Flexi Cap Fund, launched in December 2025, has returned 13.17% since inception and ranked in the top 6 of 179 funds on six-month returns.
  • The broader flexi-cap category average sits near 21% over five years, trailing the top performers by a significant margin.

India's flexi-cap mutual fund category — home to equity schemes free to invest across large, mid, and small-cap stocks — has grown increasingly competitive. Yet only three funds cleared the highest bar in July, earning five-star ratings from Value Research for superior risk-adjusted returns.

The Top Three

HDFC Flexi Cap leads the pack with a three-year CAGR of 27% and assets exceeding Rs 75,000 crore, backed by a 30-year track record and a broad portfolio. Parag Parikh Flexi Cap follows at 24.5%, distinguished by its global diversification strategy that includes US-listed stocks alongside Indian equities. Its assets crossed Rs 1.48 lakh crore by July-end, up from Rs 1.43 lakh crore in June. HDFC Retirement Savings Equity Plan rounds out the trio with a 23-24% three-year return and Rs 6,400 crore in assets, though its retirement-oriented mandate and lock-in period make it a different proposition for investors.

All three have comfortably outperformed the broader flexi-cap average, which hovers near 21% over five years.

Inside Parag Parikh's July Moves

Parag Parikh Flexi Cap made selective changes to its equity portfolio in July without adding any new stocks or exiting existing positions. The fund increased holdings in 11 companies, with Petronet LNG seeing one of the biggest additions — shares rose 52% from about 1 crore to 1.52 crore. CIE Automotive India recorded the largest percentage increase at 73%, though it remained a tiny position at 0.02% of net assets.

The fund also added to Mahanagar Gas (+20%), Indraprastha Gas (+11%), Dr Reddy's Laboratories, HCL Technologies, Maruti Suzuki, and Coal India. Its core large-cap holdings — HDFC Bank (7.55%), Power Grid (5.98%), ITC (5.74%), and ICICI Bank (5.56%) — remained unchanged in share count, with weight shifts driven purely by price movements.

"Size does not dictate success — Parag Parikh has crossed one lakh crore of assets yet still beats the pack, challenging the notion that very large funds inevitably slow down."

— Value Research analysis, July 2026

Risk-Adjusted Performance

On risk-return metrics, Parag Parikh stands out for lower volatility. Its standard deviation of 9.91% compares favourably with HDFC Flexi Cap's 13.11%, while its beta of 0.60 versus 0.82 indicates less sensitivity to market swings. Parag Parikh also edges ahead on the Sharpe ratio (0.93 vs 0.90) and Sortino ratio (1.26 vs 1.10), suggesting better returns per unit of risk taken.

HDFC Flexi Cap, however, generates a higher alpha of 5.28% compared to Parag Parikh's 4.38%, indicating stronger excess returns over its benchmark.

Abakkus: The Newcomer to Watch

Outside the five-star club, Abakkus Flexi Cap Fund has emerged as an early standout since its December 2025 launch. Managed by Sanjay Doshi and benchmarked against the BSE 500 TRI, the direct growth plan has returned 13.17% since inception with assets now at Rs 6,338 crore. On six-month returns, it ranked in the top 6 of 179 funds with a 11.30% gain — well above the category average of 3.60%.

The fund carries a lean 0.78% expense ratio for its direct plan and no exit load after three months. However, with less than a year of track record, it lacks the longer-term return data that would qualify it for Value Research ratings.

What Investors Should Consider

Flexi-cap funds offer versatility, but the data underscores wide performance dispersion within the category. The gap between the top performers and category average — roughly 4 to 6 percentage points over three years — translates into meaningful compounding differences over a decade. Parag Parikh's 10-year return of 17.49% compares with 13.66% for the BSE 500 TRI and 13.87% for the average flexi-cap fund.

However, recent performance has been more muted: Parag Parikh returned just 0.90% over one year, trailing the benchmark's 5.19%. Investors chasing long-term outperformers should weigh whether current market conditions — favouring mid and small caps that the fund underweights — represent a temporary drag or a structural shift.
nri_angle: NRI investors with Indian mutual fund accounts often use flexi-cap funds as core portfolio holdings for long-term India exposure.
